Ps1.title: What is Communication?
Ps1.content: I. What is Communication?The word communication has been derived from the Latin word 'communis' that means ‘common’. However, communication incorporates, besides commonality, the concepts of transfer, meaning and information.The Golden Rule: “You cannot not communicate”. This statement is quite often misunderstood by many of us; people may be fussy about the grammar of this sentence and that is at the cost of its spirit.Core Definition: Communication can be defined as the process through which two or more persons come to exchange ideas and understanding among them.II. Two Aspects in CommunicationTransmission: There is something, which is transmitted, such as facts, feelings, ideas, etc. This implies that there must be a receiver if communication is to occur.Understanding: The definition emphasizes the understanding element in the communication. Sharing of understanding would be possible only when the person, to whom the message is meant, understands it in the same sense in which the sender of the message wants him to understand.III. Notable Definitions of CommunicationT.S. Mathews: “Communication is something so simple and difficult that we can never put it in simple words”.Peter Little: “Communication is the process by which information is transmitted between individuals and / or organizations so that an understanding response results”.W.H. Newman and C.F. Summer Jr.: “Communication is an exchange of facts, ideas, opinions, or emotions by two or more persons”.IV. Importance of CommunicationCommunication is as important to the organization as blood is to the body. It serves as a medium through which works being done in the organization can be explained, change can be affected, a feeling of cooperation can be caused by establishing uniformity among the works of various people working in the organization, clear human relations can be established and finally the objectives of the organization are realized. “Good communication is the foundation of sound management.”Basis of decision making: Much information has to be collected for decision making and for giving final shape to any idea through communication.Effective communication promotes spirit of cooperation and coordination: An atmosphere of mutual trust and confidence between employer and employee can be possible with the existence of effective communication.Effective control: The managers get information about the work performance through communication on the basis of which they can improve upon irregularities well in time.Basis of Motivation: An efficient system of communication helps the managers in changing the point of view of the subordinates, raising their morale and presenting a basis of satisfaction.Establishment of Effective Leadership: Leadership cannot be imagined without effective communication.V. Business Communication Categories“Communication is the life blood of business. No business can develop in the absence of effective internal and external communication.”Internal Communication (Within the Organization): Effective internal communication is important because business has grown in size, business activity has become extremely complex, and it promotes a spirit of understanding and cooperation.External Communication: Includes communication with government agencies and departments on the one hand and distributors, retailers, individual customers and the general public on the other.

Ps2.title: Objectives of Communication and 7 C's of Effective Communication
Ps2.content: I. Objectives of CommunicationDefinition: The objective of communication may be defined as the passing of ideas and understanding from the sender to the target with the view to getting the desired behavioral response from the latter.Insurmountable difficulties: Finding out the actual behavioral responses and comparing these with the expected ones, in case of this continuously ongoing process, presents insurmountable difficulties.II. 7 C’s of Effective CommunicationThe 7 C’s of communication are the principles explained to effectively communicate so that the targeted group may understand the intended purpose, and offer guidelines for individuals to learn how effectively they can influence people with their own or organizational agendas.1. Completeness: It refers to a communication between sender and receiver when all the relevant information has been sent by the sender after analyzing the receiver’s mindset by ensuring no necessary information is missed during communication.2. Conciseness: During interaction, the use of accurate information in short sentences will be considered as a concise way of communication. Keyword: To the point.3. Consideration: It refers to a communication where the advantage of the receiver is given due attention by respecting the mental perception and awareness of the receiver. Keyword: About people.4. Concreteness: Concreteness refers to the specifics where interaction is performed with preciseness or by referring to statistics.5. Clarity: The endeavor for effective communication is to transfer your thoughts and ideas into the mind of the receiver using a simple, precise and easy set of words. Keyword: Simplicity.6. Courtesy: A polite word can play a prominent role in resolving disputes among people by understanding the mentality of receivers and their feelings. Keyword: Respect for Audience.7. Correctness: It refers to the factual accuracy of words used in communication between people or communicating with organizations. Keyword: Facts or Proofread.
